oracle_clues: whatsnew entry: Fixed recoverable overflow for near-minimum timestamps with microsecond and millisecond resolutions (:issue:`63278`)
PR title: BUG: handle negative overflow in Period conversion from timestamp with millisecond resolution
commit message mentions parametrized test for ms, us and ns

regression test test_construction_from_min_timestamp (GH-63278) builds Period(Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit=freq), freq=freq) and asserts no error; the failure is raised as pandas.errors.OutOfBoundsDatetime

category_specific_evidence: The PR fixes negative overflow (underflow below NPY_MIN_INT64) when converting datetimestructs to ms, us and ns resolutions in npy_datetimestruct_to_datetime, via a new helper scale_time_with_underflow_check that splits y = a*x + b = a*(x+k) + (b - a*k) with k chosen so the multiplication stays in range.

The helper computes min_scalable_time = NPY_MIN_INT64 / scale_factor and, when time < min_scalable_time, uses amount_below_threshold = time - min_scalable_time and scaled_time = scale_factor * (time - amount_below_threshold), then combines with checked_mul/checked_add.

The removed code had the explicit nanosecond special case with min_nanoseconds = NPY_MIN_INT64 + 1 and a branch for microseconds == min_nanoseconds / 1000 - 1, which is replaced by the generic helper.

The regression test test_construction_from_min_timestamp (GH-63278) was parametrized over freq in ["ms", "us", "ns"] and builds Period(Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit=freq), freq=freq), previously only covering "us"; the failure message cited was pandas.errors.OutOfBoundsDatetime for -290308-12-21 19:59:05.
Commit history includes 'fix: handle overflow in scale with amount_below_threshold mul', indicating a follow-up fix to the helper's multiplication.
reproduction_risks: The passages give no concrete numeric input values or expected outputs beyond Timestamp.min.value and the cited out-of-bounds timestamp string, so the exact failing value cannot be fully specified from the evidence.
The helper's mathematical property is stated only as a splitting identity; no explicit expected result value is given for the boundary cases.
Passages are diff fragments and may be truncated, so the full helper body and the ns path are not completely visible.
